From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>

Cc: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 29 Apr 2027 15:10:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call recap — rate limits, burst usage, and next steps

Alex — great call earlier, thanks for walking us through the Acme usage patterns. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we’re aligned: 

Summary of what you shared:
- Average monthly token volume: ~300M tokens/month (range 200M–500M)
- Target unit economics: Acme is aiming for ~$850 / 1M tokens as a goal for a committed plan
- Budget range: initial procurement target $8k–$20k / month depending on commitment and burst SLAs
- Burst behavior: frequent short spikes (10M tokens/hr) on marketing pushes, typically 1–2 hours, ~2–3x baseline for <2 hours

Open questions we said we’d follow up on:
1) Explicit overage pricing (per 1M tokens) for hosted vs committed plans
2) Quota increase / burst handling process and SLA for temporary burst grants
3) Any default throttling that would impact Acme’s UX during bursts

Attached: Acme-MAP.xlsx (mutual action plan) and a short draft pricing summary.

Next steps I propose:
- I’ll share a pricing sketch + official draft quote by EOD tomorrow
- Rafael (cc) will add technical notes on rate limits and safe burst configurations we recommend
- Alex/Priya — if you can confirm the rough monthly avg (300M) + the peak burst numbers we discussed, we’ll lock the quote and include surge language in the SOW

Thanks — talk soon.
—
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai | (415) 555-0147
Redwood Inference

Thanks Marissa — confirms on our side. A couple clarifications: 
- Target for committed price: $850 / 1M tokens (we may be able to stretch to $800 with the right SLA)
- Average monthly: ~300M tokens (we expect this to grow 15–25% q/q)
- Peak bursts: ~10M tokens/hour for short campaigns, usually <2 hours, sometimes up to 4 hours on big events.

Critical for procurement: we need a clear statement on whether bursts above our quota are allowed without throttling (even for short windows) and what the overage per 1M tokens would be if we exceed committed levels. Also want to understand how quickly we can get a temporary quota increase (e.g., same-day? 24–48h?).

If you can include an estimated monthly bill for committed vs on-demand options (based on 300M baseline + 2 short 10M bursts/month), that’ll help our finance team.

Appreciate it — Alex
VP Product, Acme Corp
alex.johnson@acme.com | (617) 555-0122

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>

Cc: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 30 Apr 2027 09:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Rate limits & overage terms — pricing sketch and answers

Alex — good questions. Below is a pricing sketch and short answers to the burst/overage items while Rafael adds the technical detail. I’ll also upload a formal draft quote (attached Draft-Quote-Acme.docx) and the pricing PDF.

Pricing sketch (illustrative):
Option A — Committed monthly (recommended)
- Commit: 300M tokens / month
- Unit price: $800 / 1M tokens
- Effective monthly: $240,000 *
- Overage: $1,100 / 1M tokens (billed on top of committed usage)

Option B — On-demand (no commit)
- Unit price: $1,600 / 1M tokens
- No monthly commitment. Bursting allowed within quota rules.

Notes on burst & quota handling:
- Default hosted project rate limits are conservative to protect multi-tenant stability. For customers with bursty traffic we: 
  - Can configure per-project token throughput quotas and short-term burst windows via the Console
  - Allow short bursts up to 3x baseline throughput for up to 10 minutes by default without throttling; sustained higher bursts are subject to throttling unless we pre-authorize a temporary quota increase
  - Temporary quota increases: typical turnaround 24–72 hours for hosted accounts; same-day emergency increases are possible but need approval from Ops and are handled case-by-case
  - We’ll add explicit contract language for surge allowances in the SOW for committed customers (helps us plan capacity and avoid throttling)

Estimated monthly cost example (300M baseline, two 10M bursts):
- Committed (300M @ $800/1M) = $240,000/month; bursts (20M @ $1,100/1M) = $22,000 => Total ~$262,000
- On-demand (320M @ $1,600/1M) = $512,000

If these numbers look directionally right, I’ll push the draft quote into DocuSign with surge language. Rafael — any notes I should fold into the SOW about safe burst settings and recommended Console settings?


Marissa

Attachments: Draft-Quote-Acme.docx, Redwood-Overage-Pricing.pdf

From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@acme.com>
Date: Fri, 30 Apr 2027 09:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Rate limits & overage terms — technical notes

Adding technical context here. TL;DR: we can support Acme’s burst profile with configuration and a small set of recommended best practices.

Technical recommendations:
- Throughput: For hosted tenants we expose two knobs: request rate (req/s) and token throughput (tokens/s). For your workloads I recommend token_throughput target = baseline_tokens_s * 1.5 and a burst_window config that allows up to 3x for short windows (10–15 minutes)
- Autoscaling: If you go with Dedicated or Reserved capacity we can size a GPU pool sized for expected peak QPS; that avoids throttling altogether but requires an upfront commit
- Batching & caching: Enable continuous batching and prefix/KV caching to reduce effective tokens per request for repeated queries — can reduce unit cost by ~10–20% depending on prompt reuse
- Quota increase process: Submit request via Console -> Support -> Quota increase; ops review includes peek at recent usage, spike history, and SSO/PO approval. Typical SLA 24–72h; for enterprise customers we can pre-approve surge windows in the contract (recommended)

I’ll include a small example of Console settings in the SOW: per-route token quota, burst_window, and emergency escalation contact. Happy to review the SOW language before it goes to legal.


Rafael Mendes
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
rafael.mendes@redwood.ai

If you can get the DocuSign out today or Monday morning that’d be ideal — procurement has a two-week review window. We’ll target a May 15 start date for the first billing cycle if all goes smoothly.

Thanks — Alex
